rubric: MODERN FRONTEND / BUILD AND PACKAGES / CHAPTER 27

slides.title: Why types
slides.main: TypeScript catches errors before running; types are erased at build time.

captions: A typo in a field or a wrong argument shows up only at run time, even in production
TypeScript describes types and checks them before execution; it is a superset of JavaScript
Types are erased at build: runs as fast as plain code

slides.title: Type basics
slides.main: string | number | boolean, arrays, objects, unions and literals; inference removes extra annotations.

captions: string, number, boolean, null, undefined; number[] is an array; object fields
string | number is one of two; "up" | "down" allows only these values
Locals are inferred; annotate at boundaries (parameters, APIs)

lines: const p: { x: number; y: number } = { x: 1, y: 2 };
function f(a: number) { return a * 2; }  // → number

slides.title: Interfaces and types
slides.main: Compatibility depends on structure, not name: anything with the needed fields fits.

captions: A field can be optional (?) or read-only (readonly)
Any value with the needed fields fits, wherever it came from
Extra field in an object literal is an error; in a ready variable it is fine

lines: const u: User = { id: 1, name: "A", age: 3 }; // ✗

slides.title: Functions and generics
slides.main: Generic T links input and output types; extends limits the allowed types.

captions: function first<T>(xs: T[]): T — result type depends on the array type
first([1, 2]) → number; first(["a"]) → string: T is inferred from arguments
T extends { length: number } — only types with a length field are allowed

lines: function len<T extends { length: number }>(x: T) {

slides.title: Type narrowing
slides.main: typeof, in, instanceof and a discriminant field narrow a union inside a branch.

captions: After a typeof check the type in the branch narrows to string
The tag field kind identifies the whole variant
All variants handled — never remains; a new variant flags the missed spot

slides.title: Utility types
slides.main: Partial, Required, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType build new types from existing ones.

captions: Partial<User> — all fields optional; Pick<User, "id"> — chosen ones
Omit<User, "email"> — without a field; Record<string, number> — a dictionary
ReturnType<typeof f> and Parameters<typeof f> derive from the function — no copying

lines: function make() { return { id: 1, ok: true }; }

slides.title: tsconfig
slides.main: strict turns on a set of strict checks; noEmit leaves tsc as a checker only.

captions: strict enables a set: noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strictFunctionTypes…
target — output language version; module/moduleResolution — import rules; noEmit — check only
extends: a shared base, and the project holds only the differences

slides.title: tsc and the build
slides.main: esbuild/SWC just strip types; tsc --noEmit does the checking; .d.ts describe library types.

captions: esbuild and SWC remove types in milliseconds but do not check correctness
tsc --noEmit — a step in the editor and CI
index.d.ts describes a library's types; @types/… — from the community (DefinitelyTyped)

lines: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.
export declare function add(a: number, b: number): number;

slides.title: Types and runtime
slides.main: Outside data is not checked by types: use unknown, a type guard and a validator like zod.

captions: A server response arrives at run time; a type "in the compiler's head" won't verify it
At the boundary accept unknown and check with a type guard or zod
as and any switch checks off — a rare exception, not a way to silence errors

lines: const user = data as User;   // a promise without checking
const x: any = data;          // types switched off

slides.title: ESLint
slides.main: ESLint finds bugs and bad practices via the AST; rules are configurable, many fix themselves.

captions: ESLint parses code into an AST and checks it with rules: eqeqeq, no-unused-vars, require-await
Each rule: off, warn or error; plugins add rules for TS and React
--fix repairs safe findings by itself

slides.title: Prettier
slides.main: Prettier formats code the same for everyone: the argument about spaces ends.

captions: Prettier prints code anew by one set of rules: width, quotes, commas
eslint-config-prettier turns off ESLint style rules so they don't conflict
Indentation and line endings for all editors — .editorconfig

slides.title: Automation
slides.main: Checks run by themselves: on changed files before a commit and in full in CI.

captions: husky + lint-staged: linter and formatter on changed files only
In CI everything in full: tsc --noEmit, eslint, prettier --check, tests
The editor shows the same errors as you type — few are left by commit time

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Types before running, a linter for bad practices, a formatter for style — all automatic.

captions: Types before running and erased at build; structural compatibility; generics; narrowing
ESLint — bad practices; Prettier — style; automation in pre-commit and CI
